title: Family site settings (site.config.json), version 1
description: Everything about how one family's site is presented. The family's facts live in data/; this file says how the engine shows them. See docs/site-config.md.

channel.description: Which releases this site takes. Most sites: stable.

version.description: Pin this site to one engine version; overrides channel.

engine.description: Which engine this site is built with.

name.description: Short name: the logo in the navigation bar and the end of page titles.

familyName.description: How Stuart names the family in a sentence: "the FitzMaurice and Andrews families".

lang.description: Language tag for the pages, e.g. en-GB.

heading.description: The heading at the top of the page, if not the engine's ("The Family Tree").

anyOf.description: The family tree page, or null for none.

tree.description: The family tree page, or null for none.

heading.description: The heading at the top of the page, if not the engine's ("The Family Tree").

anyOf.description: The family map page (needs data/places.json), or null.

map.description: The family map page (needs data/places.json), or null.

heading.description: The heading at the top of the page, if not the engine's ("The Family Tree").

anyOf.description: Stuart's page, or null for no Stuart.

ask.description: Stuart's page, or null for no Stuart.

pages.description: The site's home page and the engine's pages. A page set to null is not made, and the engine leaves out every link to it.

nav.description: The navigation bar, in order. The same on every page.

match.description: Other pages that light up this link (story pages under Branches, say).

fonts.description: A stylesheet URL for web fonts (Google Fonts, say).

stylesheets.description: The site's own stylesheets for the engine's pages, unless a page lists its own.

theme.description: CSS custom properties for the engine's look: { "--pc-accent": "#7b1f1f" }. Written into site-theme.css, which loads after the engine's styles.

dir.description: Folder of people.json, sources.json and places.json. Default data.

rootPersonId.description: Whose tree it is: the default viewpoint for relationships.

directLineLabel.description: Label for the direct line: "Sebastian's direct line".

rootOrder.description: Order of the oldest people across the tree, left to right.

regions.description: Framed groups on the tree whose link is unproven.

sides.description: Lay one partner's family on the left and the other's on the right: ids and labels.

hiddenRegions.description: Regions not drawn (people with this region stay in the data).

suspectedRelatives.description: { personId: besideId }: kept from a hidden region and drawn beside someone, with no proven link.

cardPhotos.description: set: a card shows person.photo only. best: with no photo set, the best picture in the person's media.

coupleBlocks.description: explicit: a couple who both have parents on the tree are drawn together only when the data says so (layoutJoin). auto: always, in the family of the partner on the direct line, else the husband.

legendNote.description: A sentence added to the end of the key on the family tree, in the site's own words. HTML allowed: "The earlier tree is still here."

noscript.description: What the tree page says to visitors without JavaScript after "The interactive tree needs JavaScript.", in the site's own words; HTML allowed. The default points to the home page.

tree.description: The family tree. Any key here also overrides the same key in the data's meta.

maptilerKey.description: Browser key for MapTiler (satellite and historic maps). Restrict it to the site's address in MapTiler.

googleEmbedKey.description: Browser key for Google Street View embeds. Restrict it to the site's address.

home.description: The region the map frames first; places outside it are "beyond" it.

historicMaps.description: uk-os: Ordnance Survey maps from the National Library of Scotland (Great Britain). null: no Then style.

kinAnchors.description: People the timeline relates others to: "Pat's father".

families.description: Choices in the map's Family filter.

note.description: Said after the label, e.g. "Not family".

people.description: { associateId: familyPersonId }. The associate must be in a hidden region (tree.hiddenRegions), so the tree leaves them off; the family person is who they are tied to, so a Family filter that includes that person keeps the associate's places.

associates.description: People who are not family but belong to the story, such as a business partner. Their places are drawn on the map with an associate badge, never as family, and they are not on the tree.

anchors.description: The couple at the heart of the site, left-hand side first: Stuart relates people to them ("Grandma Pat's grandfather").

homeCountry.description: For "who was born abroad?": the country that counts as home.

pages.description: The story pages Stuart reads, in reading order.

generalPages.description: Pages about many people, not one (the home page, an index of branches).

wordlikeNames.description: Surnames that are also everyday words (Field, Cousins).

familyNames.description: Words for "who were the ...": fitzmaurices, andrews.

synonyms.description: The site's own words for things, added to the words Stuart already treats as alike when searching the story pages: { "earl": ["orkney"], "newspaper": ["evening news"] }.

widget.description: The Ask Stuart button on the site's own pages.

exclude.description: Files and folders not to publish (globs from the site root).
Pages the build leaves exactly as they are.

enabled.description: Turn on the Discovery Timeline (default false). When this is false the site is built exactly as before. When it is true the build makes the page and a navigation entry, and keeps the history of finds between publications. See docs/discovery-timeline.md.

file.description: The file name of the page. Default discoveries.html.

timeline.description: The Discovery Timeline: a page of what the family has newly learned, with the history kept by the build between publications. See docs/discovery-timeline.md.

enabled.description: Turn on the site chat (default false). When this is false the site is built exactly as before.

name.description: The name on the button and in the window. Default: Guide.

greeting.description: The first message. The default says the chat answers only from this site.

placeholder.description: The hint in the question box. Default: Ask about this family.

endpoint.description: The site's own answer service. Required when enabled. An https address, with no user, password or query. The browser sends the question and the passages it found. The key stays on that service. http://127.0.0.1 and http://localhost are allowed for a local check.

pages.description: Story pages to read. When omitted, every HTML page at the top of the site is read. An empty list reads none of them (the data is still read).

skipClasses.description: Classes of page furniture the chat should not read, added to the engine's own list.

chat.description: An optional chat button. It answers from the site's own pages and records at the time of the question, through an endpoint the site runs. See docs/chat.md.
